content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am a [product_name] PLC programmer just starting with SCADA development. I am wondering which software I should install from the following options: 1. [product_name] with [company_name] [product_name] & [product_name] [version_no], 2. [product_name] RT [version_no], 3. [product_name] [version_no], 4. [product_name] [version_no], 5. [product_name] RT Advanced [version_no]. My knowledge of SCADA is limited and I have access to only certain software through my college program. I found information stating that the communication driver for [product_name] is available starting with version 12 of [product_name], but also read that the communication driver is only available for [product_name] RT Advanced, not Professional, in a forum discussion ([url]). Could someone help me clarify so I can begin learning SCADA development with this setup? Looking forward to your help. Thank you and regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. About connecting [product_name] to [product_name] [version_no], you should not worry too much about this. The communication driver for [product_name] is available in all [product_name] variants, including Basic, Advanced/Comfort, or Professional. Since [product_name] [version_no], the communication driver for [product_name] exists; before that, you had to use another driver. You do not need a server connection in the software; only in [product_name] do you need to create a connection (check the attached screenshot for a V13 project). If you need an example, post more details: - Which [product_name] version and variant. - Which LSC version. - Which [product_name] (Order number).

Thank you for your quick reply. I have another question: Is [product_name] Professional and [product_name] RunTime (RT) Professional the same thing? Should I choose [product_name] Professional [version_no] or [product_name] RunTime (RT) Professional [version_no]? Is [product_name] RunTime included with [product_name] Professional, or do I need to install both? Thanks and regards, [user_name]

There is a distinction: [product_name] is the engineering software for creating visualizations, and [product_name] RT is the runtime for displaying them. [product_name] RT is already integrated into every [company_name] panel and does not need separate installation. However, if you plan to use a standard PC for visualization instead of a panel, you must install [product_name] RT on that PC.

Thank you. The list of software provided to me includes: 1. [company_name] [product_name] & [product_name] [version_no], 2. [company_name] [product_name] RunTime (RT) Professional [version_no]. I am unsure whether installing the first option will automatically install the second, or if they must be installed separately. Please advise. Thanks and regards, [user_name]

It seems the difference between [product_name] and [product_name] RT is still unclear. [product_name] is for creating visualizations, while [product_name] RT is needed to run them on a PC. If you use a [company_name] panel, the runtime is already included and does not require separate installation. Both are standalone software products and must be installed individually.
Thank you for the explanation. I will install both as advised. Thanks again for clearing up my confusion.

analysis.insight_summary: A beginner in SCADA development wanted advice about which [company_name] SCADA software to install for use with [product_name]. Their main confusion was about the difference between [product_name] Professional and [product_name] RunTime (RT) Professional, and which combinations are needed for PC-based visualization. Experienced users explained that [product_name] is for engineering projects and [product_name] RT is for runtime visualization on a PC, and clarified the distinction between engineering and runtime environments and software bundling. The lack of intuitive documentation led to repeated queries until the user understood the product differences.
analysis.user_expectations: User is seeking clear instructions on which version(s) of [product_name] and related products should be installed, including details on software bundling. They expect easily understandable, beginner-friendly advice about product differences and installation requirements.
